outcome: bleeding from the cord puncture site
cohort: 119 mothers with 154 fetuses who underwent intrauterine transfusion (IUT) for Rh alloimmunization between January 2009 and August 2019 at a tertiary care center
finding: Intrauterine transfusion is an effective treatment for Rh alloimmunization, with a high survival rate (around 90%), but complications, including fetal bradycardia, bleeding, contractions, intrauterine fetal death, and neonatal death, can still occur.
mod_finding: Eight (5.2%) of the mothers in the study underwent cesarean delivery due to IUT-specific complications such as post-procedure fetal bradycardia.
